Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

  • Kei Okada

Authors

No additional authors.
jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

Python: jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat 

from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION

if __name__ == '__main__':
    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)
  ROS1 ROS2
get_param(node, '~name', default), has_param rospy.get_param declares a (dynamically typed) parameter
init_node(name, anonymous=False, multi_threaded=False) rospy.init_node, returns None rclpy.init() + a new node, returned (multi_threaded: see below)
spin(node), spin_once(node, timeout_sec), shutdown(node) (after an own while not is_shutdown(node) loop) rospy.spin, rospy.sleep, - spin_and_shutdown, rclpy.spin_once, cleanup
loginfo/logwarn/logerr/logdebug/logfatal(node, msg) rospy.log* node.get_logger().* (msg must be a str; node=None uses a logger named after the script)
loginfo/logwarn/logerr_throttle(node, period, msg), loginfo/logwarn/logerr_once(node, msg) like rospy.log*_throttle/_once like throttle_duration_sec=/once=True (per call site, done in compat)
create_publisher(node, topic, type, queue_size=1, latch=False) rospy.Publisher node.create_publisher (latch: transient-local QoS)
create_subscription(node, topic, type, cb, queue_size=None, latch=False) rospy.Subscriber (None: unbounded) node.create_subscription (None: depth 1; latch: transient-local QoS; ~foo -> ~/foo)
wait_for_service(node, name, type, timeout) (returns bool), set_param(node, name, value) rospy.wait_for_service, rospy.set_param a client’s wait_for_service, node.set_parameters
create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor
init_node(name, multi_threaded=True), for callbacks waiting for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic) ignored (as above) create_* default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor
create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Action types: pass FooAction/FooGoal on ROS1 and Foo/Foo.Goal on ROS2; timeouts are in seconds on both. actionlib/dynamic_reconfigure are imported lazily, so depend on them in your own package.

Packages outside jsk_common

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat is only released with jsk_common >= 3.0, which is not available for every ROS1 distro. Depend on it for ROS2 only and fall back to rospy when it can not be imported, listing just the functions you use:

<exec_depend condition="$ROS_VERSION == 2">jsk_ros1_ros2_compat</exec_depend>


try:
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION
except ImportError:
    # jsk_common < 3.0 has no jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, so this is ROS1 only:
    # forward ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) to rospy.xxx(...)
    import rospy
    ROS_VERSION = 1
    class ros_compat(object):
        get_param = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.get_param(*args, **kwargs))
        loginfo = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.loginfo(*args, **kwargs))

Or, to keep the original rospy code untouched for its ROS1 users, add a jsk_ros1_ros2_compat version next to it and choose by whether jsk_ros1_ros2_compat can be imported (not by ROS_VERSION):

CHANGELOG

Changelog for package jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

3.0.3 (2026-11-03)

  • Merge pull request #1835 from k-okada/ros-version-fallback-ament Fix ROS2 buildfarm binary jobs: ROS_VERSION without ros_environment, boost for jsk_topic_tools

  • Merge pull request #1834 from pazeshun/array-to-heatmap [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_rosbag_tools] Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

  • Guess ROS_VERSION from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH when unset, depend on ros_environment The ROS2 binary jobs of the buildfarm failed at find_package(catkin): they install only the build dependencies, none of which pulls in ros_environment, so $ENV{ROS_VERSION} is empty and the fallback at the top of CMakeLists.txt chose ROS1.

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. Applies to jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_tools, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_common, jsk_data, jsk_rosbag_tools, dynamic_tf_publisher, audio_video_recorder and image_view2. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Merge pull request #1 from k-okada/array-to-heatmap-old-distros Support indigo/kinetic in array heatmap tools (OpenCV 2.4, numpy < 1.9, rosbag < 1.13)

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] rosbag: raw messages with connection headers on rosbag < 1.13 rosbag of indigo/kinetic has neither read_messages(..., return_connection_header=) nor write(..., connection_header=), which failed test_add_heatmap on the kinetic CI. There, read_raw_messages() takes the header of each topic's connection from the bag, and write_raw() registers a new topic's connection with the given header before writing, as write(..., connection_header=) does on newer rosbag. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

    • Render numeric MultiArray and scalar Image topics as heatmap images with optional cell values and configurable color scales
    • Add heatmap topics to bags while preserving original messages, recording timestamps, and connection or QoS metadata
    • Extend the compatibility layer with raw bag I/O and shared message type helpers
    • Add installation rules, documentation, and tests for both ROS versions

  • Merge pull request #1833 from k-okada/release-3.0.2 3.0.2

  • Contributors: Kei Okada, Shun Hasegawa

3.0.2 (2026-11-02)

  • Merge pull request #1831 from k-okada/ros2-compat-fixes [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] fix queue_size/shutdown/throttle; add init_node/spin, latch, actionlib, reconfigure, uv venv helpers

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] spin() with an own executor, not rclpy's global one rclpy.spin(node) spins rclpy's global executor, so a callback could not call a library which spins its own node with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(), such as sound_play's SoundClient(node, blocking=True).say() ('Executor is already spinning'). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add callback_group to create_* (ROS2

Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

Authors

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

Python: jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat 

from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION

if __name__ == '__main__':
    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)
  ROS1 ROS2
get_param(node, '~name', default), has_param rospy.get_param declares a (dynamically typed) parameter
init_node(name, anonymous=False, multi_threaded=False) rospy.init_node, returns None rclpy.init() + a new node, returned (multi_threaded: see below)
spin(node), spin_once(node, timeout_sec), shutdown(node) (after an own while not is_shutdown(node) loop) rospy.spin, rospy.sleep, - spin_and_shutdown, rclpy.spin_once, cleanup
loginfo/logwarn/logerr/logdebug/logfatal(node, msg) rospy.log* node.get_logger().* (msg must be a str; node=None uses a logger named after the script)
loginfo/logwarn/logerr_throttle(node, period, msg), loginfo/logwarn/logerr_once(node, msg) like rospy.log*_throttle/_once like throttle_duration_sec=/once=True (per call site, done in compat)
create_publisher(node, topic, type, queue_size=1, latch=False) rospy.Publisher node.create_publisher (latch: transient-local QoS)
create_subscription(node, topic, type, cb, queue_size=None, latch=False) rospy.Subscriber (None: unbounded) node.create_subscription (None: depth 1; latch: transient-local QoS; ~foo -> ~/foo)
wait_for_service(node, name, type, timeout) (returns bool), set_param(node, name, value) rospy.wait_for_service, rospy.set_param a client’s wait_for_service, node.set_parameters
create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor
init_node(name, multi_threaded=True), for callbacks waiting for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic) ignored (as above) create_* default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor
create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Action types: pass FooAction/FooGoal on ROS1 and Foo/Foo.Goal on ROS2; timeouts are in seconds on both. actionlib/dynamic_reconfigure are imported lazily, so depend on them in your own package.

Packages outside jsk_common

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat is only released with jsk_common >= 3.0, which is not available for every ROS1 distro. Depend on it for ROS2 only and fall back to rospy when it can not be imported, listing just the functions you use:

<exec_depend condition="$ROS_VERSION == 2">jsk_ros1_ros2_compat</exec_depend>


try:
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION
except ImportError:
    # jsk_common < 3.0 has no jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, so this is ROS1 only:
    # forward ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) to rospy.xxx(...)
    import rospy
    ROS_VERSION = 1
    class ros_compat(object):
        get_param = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.get_param(*args, **kwargs))
        loginfo = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.loginfo(*args, **kwargs))

Or, to keep the original rospy code untouched for its ROS1 users, add a jsk_ros1_ros2_compat version next to it and choose by whether jsk_ros1_ros2_compat can be imported (not by ROS_VERSION):

CHANGELOG

Changelog for package jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

3.0.3 (2026-11-03)

  • Merge pull request #1835 from k-okada/ros-version-fallback-ament Fix ROS2 buildfarm binary jobs: ROS_VERSION without ros_environment, boost for jsk_topic_tools

  • Merge pull request #1834 from pazeshun/array-to-heatmap [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_rosbag_tools] Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

  • Guess ROS_VERSION from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH when unset, depend on ros_environment The ROS2 binary jobs of the buildfarm failed at find_package(catkin): they install only the build dependencies, none of which pulls in ros_environment, so $ENV{ROS_VERSION} is empty and the fallback at the top of CMakeLists.txt chose ROS1.

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. Applies to jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_tools, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_common, jsk_data, jsk_rosbag_tools, dynamic_tf_publisher, audio_video_recorder and image_view2. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Merge pull request #1 from k-okada/array-to-heatmap-old-distros Support indigo/kinetic in array heatmap tools (OpenCV 2.4, numpy < 1.9, rosbag < 1.13)

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] rosbag: raw messages with connection headers on rosbag < 1.13 rosbag of indigo/kinetic has neither read_messages(..., return_connection_header=) nor write(..., connection_header=), which failed test_add_heatmap on the kinetic CI. There, read_raw_messages() takes the header of each topic's connection from the bag, and write_raw() registers a new topic's connection with the given header before writing, as write(..., connection_header=) does on newer rosbag. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

    • Render numeric MultiArray and scalar Image topics as heatmap images with optional cell values and configurable color scales
    • Add heatmap topics to bags while preserving original messages, recording timestamps, and connection or QoS metadata
    • Extend the compatibility layer with raw bag I/O and shared message type helpers
    • Add installation rules, documentation, and tests for both ROS versions

  • Merge pull request #1833 from k-okada/release-3.0.2 3.0.2

  • Contributors: Kei Okada, Shun Hasegawa

3.0.2 (2026-11-02)

  • Merge pull request #1831 from k-okada/ros2-compat-fixes [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] fix queue_size/shutdown/throttle; add init_node/spin, latch, actionlib, reconfigure, uv venv helpers

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] spin() with an own executor, not rclpy's global one rclpy.spin(node) spins rclpy's global executor, so a callback could not call a library which spins its own node with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(), such as sound_play's SoundClient(node, blocking=True).say() ('Executor is already spinning'). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add callback_group to create_* (ROS2

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat is only released with jsk_common >= 3.0, which is not available for every ROS1 distro. Depend on it for ROS2 only and fall back to rospy when it can not be imported, listing just the functions you use:

<exec_depend condition="$ROS_VERSION == 2">jsk_ros1_ros2_compat</exec_depend>


try:
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION
except ImportError:
    # jsk_common < 3.0 has no jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, so this is ROS1 only:
    # forward ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) to rospy.xxx(...)
    import rospy
    ROS_VERSION = 1
    class ros_compat(object):
        get_param = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.get_param(*args, **kwargs))
        loginfo = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.loginfo(*args, **kwargs))

Changelog for package jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

3.0.3 (2026-11-03)

  • Merge pull request #1835 from k-okada/ros-version-fallback-ament Fix ROS2 buildfarm binary jobs: ROS_VERSION without ros_environment, boost for jsk_topic_tools

  • Merge pull request #1834 from pazeshun/array-to-heatmap [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_rosbag_tools] Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

  • Guess ROS_VERSION from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH when unset, depend on ros_environment The ROS2 binary jobs of the buildfarm failed at find_package(catkin): they install only the build dependencies, none of which pulls in ros_environment, so $ENV{ROS_VERSION} is empty and the fallback at the top of CMakeLists.txt chose ROS1.

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. Applies to jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_tools, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_common, jsk_data, jsk_rosbag_tools, dynamic_tf_publisher, audio_video_recorder and image_view2. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Merge pull request #1 from k-okada/array-to-heatmap-old-distros Support indigo/kinetic in array heatmap tools (OpenCV 2.4, numpy < 1.9, rosbag < 1.13)

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] rosbag: raw messages with connection headers on rosbag < 1.13 rosbag of indigo/kinetic has neither read_messages(..., return_connection_header=) nor write(..., connection_header=), which failed test_add_heatmap on the kinetic CI. There, read_raw_messages() takes the header of each topic's connection from the bag, and write_raw() registers a new topic's connection with the given header before writing, as write(..., connection_header=) does on newer rosbag. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

    • Render numeric MultiArray and scalar Image topics as heatmap images with optional cell values and configurable color scales
    • Add heatmap topics to bags while preserving original messages, recording timestamps, and connection or QoS metadata
    • Extend the compatibility layer with raw bag I/O and shared message type helpers
    • Add installation rules, documentation, and tests for both ROS versions

  • Merge pull request #1833 from k-okada/release-3.0.2 3.0.2

  • Contributors: Kei Okada, Shun Hasegawa

3.0.2 (2026-11-02)

  • Merge pull request #1831 from k-okada/ros2-compat-fixes [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] fix queue_size/shutdown/throttle; add init_node/spin, latch, actionlib, reconfigure, uv venv helpers

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] spin() with an own executor, not rclpy's global one rclpy.spin(node) spins rclpy's global executor, so a callback could not call a library which spins its own node with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(), such as sound_play's SoundClient(node, blocking=True).say() ('Executor is already spinning'). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

  • Kei Okada

Authors

No additional authors.
jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)

loginfo/logwarn/logerr/logdebug/logfatal(node, msg) rospy.log* node.get_logger().* (msg must be a str; node=None uses a logger named after the script)
loginfo/logwarn/logerr_throttle(node, period, msg), loginfo/logwarn/logerr_once(node, msg) like rospy.log*_throttle/_once like throttle_duration_sec=/once=True (per call site, done in compat)
create_publisher(node, topic, type, queue_size=1, latch=False) rospy.Publisher node.create_publisher (latch: transient-local QoS)
create_subscription(node, topic, type, cb, queue_size=None, latch=False) rospy.Subscriber (None: unbounded) node.create_subscription (None: depth 1; latch: transient-local QoS; ~foo -> ~/foo)
wait_for_service(node, name, type, timeout) (returns bool), set_param(node, name, value) rospy.wait_for_service, rospy.set_param a client’s wait_for_service, node.set_parameters
create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor
init_node(name, multi_threaded=True), for callbacks waiting for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic) ignored (as above) create_* default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor
create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Action types: pass FooAction/FooGoal on ROS1 and Foo/Foo.Goal on ROS2; timeouts are in seconds on both. actionlib/dynamic_reconfigure are imported lazily, so depend on them in your own package.

Packages outside jsk_common

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat is only released with jsk_common >= 3.0, which is not available for every ROS1 distro. Depend on it for ROS2 only and fall back to rospy when it can not be imported, listing just the functions you use:

<exec_depend condition="$ROS_VERSION == 2">jsk_ros1_ros2_compat</exec_depend>


try:
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION
except ImportError:
    # jsk_common < 3.0 has no jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, so this is ROS1 only:
    # forward ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) to rospy.xxx(...)
    import rospy
    ROS_VERSION = 1
    class ros_compat(object):
        get_param = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.get_param(*args, **kwargs))
        loginfo = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.loginfo(*args, **kwargs))

Changelog for package jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

3.0.3 (2026-11-03)

  • Merge pull request #1835 from k-okada/ros-version-fallback-ament Fix ROS2 buildfarm binary jobs: ROS_VERSION without ros_environment, boost for jsk_topic_tools

  • Merge pull request #1834 from pazeshun/array-to-heatmap [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_rosbag_tools] Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

  • Guess ROS_VERSION from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH when unset, depend on ros_environment The ROS2 binary jobs of the buildfarm failed at find_package(catkin): they install only the build dependencies, none of which pulls in ros_environment, so $ENV{ROS_VERSION} is empty and the fallback at the top of CMakeLists.txt chose ROS1.

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. Applies to jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_tools, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_common, jsk_data, jsk_rosbag_tools, dynamic_tf_publisher, audio_video_recorder and image_view2. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Merge pull request #1 from k-okada/array-to-heatmap-old-distros Support indigo/kinetic in array heatmap tools (OpenCV 2.4, numpy < 1.9, rosbag < 1.13)

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] rosbag: raw messages with connection headers on rosbag < 1.13 rosbag of indigo/kinetic has neither read_messages(..., return_connection_header=) nor write(..., connection_header=), which failed test_add_heatmap on the kinetic CI. There, read_raw_messages() takes the header of each topic's connection from the bag, and write_raw() registers a new topic's connection with the given header before writing, as write(..., connection_header=) does on newer rosbag. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

    • Render numeric MultiArray and scalar Image topics as heatmap images with optional cell values and configurable color scales
    • Add heatmap topics to bags while preserving original messages, recording timestamps, and connection or QoS metadata
    • Extend the compatibility layer with raw bag I/O and shared message type helpers
    • Add installation rules, documentation, and tests for both ROS versions

  • Merge pull request #1833 from k-okada/release-3.0.2 3.0.2

  • Contributors: Kei Okada, Shun Hasegawa

3.0.2 (2026-11-02)

  • Merge pull request #1831 from k-okada/ros2-compat-fixes [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] fix queue_size/shutdown/throttle; add init_node/spin, latch, actionlib, reconfigure, uv venv helpers

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] spin() with an own executor, not rclpy's global one rclpy.spin(node) spins rclpy's global executor, so a callback could not call a library which spins its own node with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(), such as sound_play's SoundClient(node, blocking=True).say() ('Executor is already spinning'). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

  • Kei Okada

Authors

No additional authors.
jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

Python: jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat 

from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION

if __name__ == '__main__':
    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)

create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor

create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Action types: pass FooAction/FooGoal on ROS1 and Foo/Foo.Goal on ROS2; timeouts are in seconds on both. actionlib/dynamic_reconfigure are imported lazily, so depend on them in your own package.

Packages outside jsk_common

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat is only released with jsk_common >= 3.0, which is not available for every ROS1 distro. Depend on it for ROS2 only and fall back to rospy when it can not be imported, listing just the functions you use:

<exec_depend condition="$ROS_VERSION == 2">jsk_ros1_ros2_compat</exec_depend>


try:
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION
except ImportError:
    # jsk_common < 3.0 has no jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, so this is ROS1 only:
    # forward ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) to rospy.xxx(...)
    import rospy
    ROS_VERSION = 1
    class ros_compat(object):
        get_param = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.get_param(*args, **kwargs))
        loginfo = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.loginfo(*args, **kwargs))

3.0.3 (2026-11-03)

  • Merge pull request #1835 from k-okada/ros-version-fallback-ament Fix ROS2 buildfarm binary jobs: ROS_VERSION without ros_environment, boost for jsk_topic_tools

  • Merge pull request #1834 from pazeshun/array-to-heatmap [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_rosbag_tools] Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

  • Guess ROS_VERSION from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH when unset, depend on ros_environment The ROS2 binary jobs of the buildfarm failed at find_package(catkin): they install only the build dependencies, none of which pulls in ros_environment, so $ENV{ROS_VERSION} is empty and the fallback at the top of CMakeLists.txt chose ROS1.

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. Applies to jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_tools, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_common, jsk_data, jsk_rosbag_tools, dynamic_tf_publisher, audio_video_recorder and image_view2. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Merge pull request #1 from k-okada/array-to-heatmap-old-distros Support indigo/kinetic in array heatmap tools (OpenCV 2.4, numpy < 1.9, rosbag < 1.13)

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] rosbag: raw messages with connection headers on rosbag < 1.13 rosbag of indigo/kinetic has neither read_messages(..., return_connection_header=) nor write(..., connection_header=), which failed test_add_heatmap on the kinetic CI. There, read_raw_messages() takes the header of each topic's connection from the bag, and write_raw() registers a new topic's connection with the given header before writing, as write(..., connection_header=) does on newer rosbag. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

    • Render numeric MultiArray and scalar Image topics as heatmap images with optional cell values and configurable color scales
    • Add heatmap topics to bags while preserving original messages, recording timestamps, and connection or QoS metadata
    • Extend the compatibility layer with raw bag I/O and shared message type helpers
    • Add installation rules, documentation, and tests for both ROS versions

  • Merge pull request #1833 from k-okada/release-3.0.2 3.0.2

  • Contributors: Kei Okada, Shun Hasegawa

3.0.2 (2026-11-02)

  • Merge pull request #1831 from k-okada/ros2-compat-fixes [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] fix queue_size/shutdown/throttle; add init_node/spin, latch, actionlib, reconfigure, uv venv helpers

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] spin() with an own executor, not rclpy's global one rclpy.spin(node) spins rclpy's global executor, so a callback could not call a library which spins its own node with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(), such as sound_play's SoundClient(node, blocking=True).say() ('Executor is already spinning'). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

  • Kei Okada

Authors

No additional authors.
jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

Python: jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat 

from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION

if __name__ == '__main__':
    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)
  ROS1 ROS2
get_param(node, '~name', default), has_param rospy.get_param declares a (dynamically typed) parameter
init_node(name, anonymous=False, multi_threaded=False) rospy.init_node, returns None rclpy.init() + a new node, returned (multi_threaded: see below)
spin(node), spin_once(node, timeout_sec), shutdown(node) (after an own while not is_shutdown(node) loop) rospy.spin, rospy.sleep, - spin_and_shutdown, rclpy.spin_once, cleanup
loginfo/logwarn/logerr/logdebug/logfatal(node, msg) rospy.log* node.get_logger().* (msg must be a str; node=None uses a logger named after the script)
loginfo/logwarn/logerr_throttle(node, period, msg), loginfo/logwarn/logerr_once(node, msg) like rospy.log*_throttle/_once like throttle_duration_sec=/once=True (per call site, done in compat)
create_publisher(node, topic, type, queue_size=1, latch=False) rospy.Publisher node.create_publisher (latch: transient-local QoS)
create_subscription(node, topic, type, cb, queue_size=None, latch=False) rospy.Subscriber (None: unbounded) node.create_subscription (None: depth 1; latch: transient-local QoS; ~foo -> ~/foo)
wait_for_service(node, name, type, timeout) (returns bool), set_param(node, name, value) rospy.wait_for_service, rospy.set_param a client’s wait_for_service, node.set_parameters
create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor
init_node(name, multi_threaded=True), for callbacks waiting for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic) ignored (as above) create_* default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor
create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Changelog for package jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

3.0.3 (2026-11-03)

  • Merge pull request #1835 from k-okada/ros-version-fallback-ament Fix ROS2 buildfarm binary jobs: ROS_VERSION without ros_environment, boost for jsk_topic_tools

  • Merge pull request #1834 from pazeshun/array-to-heatmap [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_rosbag_tools] Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

  • Guess ROS_VERSION from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH when unset, depend on ros_environment The ROS2 binary jobs of the buildfarm failed at find_package(catkin): they install only the build dependencies, none of which pulls in ros_environment, so $ENV{ROS_VERSION} is empty and the fallback at the top of CMakeLists.txt chose ROS1.

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. Applies to jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_tools, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_common, jsk_data, jsk_rosbag_tools, dynamic_tf_publisher, audio_video_recorder and image_view2. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • Merge pull request #1 from k-okada/array-to-heatmap-old-distros Support indigo/kinetic in array heatmap tools (OpenCV 2.4, numpy < 1.9, rosbag < 1.13)

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] rosbag: raw messages with connection headers on rosbag < 1.13 rosbag of indigo/kinetic has neither read_messages(..., return_connection_header=) nor write(..., connection_header=), which failed test_add_heatmap on the kinetic CI. There, read_raw_messages() takes the header of each topic's connection from the bag, and write_raw() registers a new topic's connection with the given header before writing, as write(..., connection_header=) does on newer rosbag. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

    • Extend the compatibility layer with raw bag I/O and shared message type helpers
    • Add installation rules, documentation, and tests for both ROS versions

  • Merge pull request #1833 from k-okada/release-3.0.2 3.0.2

  • Contributors: Kei Okada, Shun Hasegawa

3.0.2 (2026-11-02)

  • Merge pull request #1831 from k-okada/ros2-compat-fixes [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] fix queue_size/shutdown/throttle; add init_node/spin, latch, actionlib, reconfigure, uv venv helpers

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] spin() with an own executor, not rclpy's global one rclpy.spin(node) spins rclpy's global executor, so a callback could not call a library which spins its own node with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(), such as sound_play's SoundClient(node, blocking=True).say() ('Executor is already spinning'). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

Authors

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

Python: jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat 

from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION

if __name__ == '__main__':
    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)
  ROS1 ROS2
get_param(node, '~name', default), has_param rospy.get_param declares a (dynamically typed) parameter
init_node(name, anonymous=False, multi_threaded=False) rospy.init_node, returns None rclpy.init() + a new node, returned (multi_threaded: see below)
spin(node), spin_once(node, timeout_sec), shutdown(node) (after an own while not is_shutdown(node) loop) rospy.spin, rospy.sleep, - spin_and_shutdown, rclpy.spin_once, cleanup
loginfo/logwarn/logerr/logdebug/logfatal(node, msg) rospy.log* node.get_logger().* (msg must be a str; node=None uses a logger named after the script)
loginfo/logwarn/logerr_throttle(node, period, msg), loginfo/logwarn/logerr_once(node, msg) like rospy.log*_throttle/_once like throttle_duration_sec=/once=True (per call site, done in compat)
create_publisher(node, topic, type, queue_size=1, latch=False) rospy.Publisher node.create_publisher (latch: transient-local QoS)
create_subscription(node, topic, type, cb, queue_size=None, latch=False) rospy.Subscriber (None: unbounded) node.create_subscription (None: depth 1; latch: transient-local QoS; ~foo -> ~/foo)
wait_for_service(node, name, type, timeout) (returns bool), set_param(node, name, value) rospy.wait_for_service, rospy.set_param a client’s wait_for_service, node.set_parameters
create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor
init_node(name, multi_threaded=True), for callbacks waiting for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic) ignored (as above) create_* default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor
create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Action types: pass FooAction/FooGoal on ROS1 and Foo/Foo.Goal on ROS2; timeouts are in seconds on both. actionlib/dynamic_reconfigure are imported lazily, so depend on them in your own package.

3.0.3 (2026-11-03)

  • Merge pull request #1835 from k-okada/ros-version-fallback-ament Fix ROS2 buildfarm binary jobs: ROS_VERSION without ros_environment, boost for jsk_topic_tools

  • Guess ROS_VERSION from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH when unset, depend on ros_environment The ROS2 binary jobs of the buildfarm failed at find_package(catkin): they install only the build dependencies, none of which pulls in ros_environment, so $ENV{ROS_VERSION} is empty and the fallback at the top of CMakeLists.txt chose ROS1.

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. There, read_raw_messages() takes the header of each topic's connection from the bag, and write_raw() registers a new topic's connection with the given header before writing, as write(..., connection_header=) does on newer rosbag.     • Add installation rules, documentation, and tests for both ROS versions

3.0.2 (2026-11-02)

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] spin() with an own executor, not rclpy's global one rclpy.spin(node) spins rclpy's global executor, so a callback could not call a library which spins its own node with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(), such as sound_play's SoundClient(node, blocking=True).say() ('Executor is already spinning'). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

  • Kei Okada

Authors

No additional authors.
jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

Python: jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat 

from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION

if __name__ == '__main__':
    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)
  ROS1 ROS2
get_param(node, '~name', default), has_param rospy.get_param declares a (dynamically typed) parameter
init_node(name, anonymous=False, multi_threaded=False) rospy.init_node, returns None rclpy.init() + a new node, returned (multi_threaded: see below)
spin(node), spin_once(node, timeout_sec), shutdown(node) (after an own while not is_shutdown(node) loop) rospy.spin, rospy.sleep, - spin_and_shutdown, rclpy.spin_once, cleanup
loginfo/logwarn/logerr/logdebug/logfatal(node, msg) rospy.log* node.get_logger().* (msg must be a str; node=None uses a logger named after the script)
loginfo/logwarn/logerr_throttle(node, period, msg), loginfo/logwarn/logerr_once(node, msg) like rospy.log*_throttle/_once like throttle_duration_sec=/once=True (per call site, done in compat)
create_publisher(node, topic, type, queue_size=1, latch=False) rospy.Publisher node.create_publisher (latch: transient-local QoS)
create_subscription(node, topic, type, cb, queue_size=None, latch=False) rospy.Subscriber (None: unbounded) node.create_subscription (None: depth 1; latch: transient-local QoS; ~foo -> ~/foo)
wait_for_service(node, name, type, timeout) (returns bool), set_param(node, name, value) rospy.wait_for_service, rospy.set_param a client’s wait_for_service, node.set_parameters
create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor
init_node(name, multi_threaded=True), for callbacks waiting for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic) ignored (as above) create_* default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor
create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Action types: pass FooAction/FooGoal on ROS1 and Foo/Foo.Goal on ROS2; timeouts are in seconds on both. actionlib/dynamic_reconfigure are imported lazily, so depend on them in your own package.

Packages outside jsk_common

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat is only released with jsk_common >= 3.0, which is not available for every ROS1 distro. Depend on it for ROS2 only and fall back to rospy when it can not be imported, listing just the functions you use:

<exec_depend condition="$ROS_VERSION == 2">jsk_ros1_ros2_compat</exec_depend>


try:
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION
except ImportError:
    # jsk_common < 3.0 has no jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, so this is ROS1 only:
    # forward ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) to rospy.xxx(...)
    import rospy
    ROS_VERSION = 1
    class ros_compat(object):
        get_param = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.get_param(*args, **kwargs))
        loginfo = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.loginfo(*args, **kwargs))

Or, to keep the original rospy code untouched for its ROS1 users, add a jsk_ros1_ros2_compat version next to it and choose by whether jsk_ros1_ros2_compat can be imported (not by ROS_VERSION):

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

  • Kei Okada

Authors

No additional authors.
jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

Python: jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat 

from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION

if __name__ == '__main__':
    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)
  ROS1 ROS2
get_param(node, '~name', default), has_param rospy.get_param declares a (dynamically typed) parameter
init_node(name, anonymous=False, multi_threaded=False) rospy.init_node, returns None rclpy.init() + a new node, returned (multi_threaded: see below)
spin(node), spin_once(node, timeout_sec), shutdown(node) (after an own while not is_shutdown(node) loop) rospy.spin, rospy.sleep, - spin_and_shutdown, rclpy.spin_once, cleanup
loginfo/logwarn/logerr/logdebug/logfatal(node, msg) rospy.log* node.get_logger().* (msg must be a str; node=None uses a logger named after the script)
loginfo/logwarn/logerr_throttle(node, period, msg), loginfo/logwarn/logerr_once(node, msg) like rospy.log*_throttle/_once like throttle_duration_sec=/once=True (per call site, done in compat)
create_publisher(node, topic, type, queue_size=1, latch=False) rospy.Publisher node.create_publisher (latch: transient-local QoS)
create_subscription(node, topic, type, cb, queue_size=None, latch=False) rospy.Subscriber (None: unbounded) node.create_subscription (None: depth 1; latch: transient-local QoS; ~foo -> ~/foo)
wait_for_service(node, name, type, timeout) (returns bool), set_param(node, name, value) rospy.wait_for_service, rospy.set_param a client’s wait_for_service, node.set_parameters
create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor
init_node(name, multi_threaded=True), for callbacks waiting for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic) ignored (as above) create_* default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor
create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Action types: pass FooAction/FooGoal on ROS1 and Foo/Foo.Goal on ROS2; timeouts are in seconds on both. actionlib/dynamic_reconfigure are imported lazily, so depend on them in your own package.

Packages outside jsk_common

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat is only released with jsk_common >= 3.0, which is not available for every ROS1 distro. Depend on it for ROS2 only and fall back to rospy when it can not be imported, listing just the functions you use:

<exec_depend condition="$ROS_VERSION == 2">jsk_ros1_ros2_compat</exec_depend>


try:
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION
except ImportError:
    # jsk_common < 3.0 has no jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, so this is ROS1 only:
    # forward ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) to rospy.xxx(...)
    import rospy
    ROS_VERSION = 1
    class ros_compat(object):
        get_param = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.get_param(*args, **kwargs))
        loginfo = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.loginfo(*args, **kwargs))

Or, to keep the original rospy code untouched for its ROS1 users, add a jsk_ros1_ros2_compat version next to it and choose by whether jsk_ros1_ros2_compat can be imported (not by ROS_VERSION):

```python try:

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] spin() with an own executor, not rclpy's global one rclpy.spin(node) spins rclpy's global executor, so a callback could not call a library which spins its own node with rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(), such as sound_play's SoundClient(node, blocking=True).say() ('Executor is already spinning'). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] return from wait_for_result() on shutdown On ROS2, the result of a goal never comes after SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a callback blocked in send_goal_and_wait()/wait_for_result() without a timeout kept its executor thread, and so the process, alive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

  • [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat] add init_node(..., multi_threaded=True) For nodes whose callbacks wait for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic or an action result), which works on rospy, as it runs each callback in its own thread, but deadlocks with rclpy's single-threaded executor and default (mutually exclusive) callback group. With multi_threaded=True, create_*() of the node default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor, so the node code needs no rclpy specific executor/callback group; ignored on ROS1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<noreply@anthropic.com>>

Package Description

Shared ROS1(roscpp/rospy)/ROS2(rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers used across jsk_common's ROS2-ported packages, so that individual packages don't each maintain their own copy.

Maintainers

  • Kei Okada

Authors

No additional authors.
jsk_ros1_ros2_compat/README.md

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

Shared ROS1 (roscpp/rospy) / ROS2 (rclcpp/rclpy) compatibility helpers, so that a package can keep one source tree that builds and runs on both, with the ROS1 code left as close to the original as possible.

Porting style

  • One package.xml / CMakeLists.txt branched on $ROS_VERSION.
    • package.xml: condition="$ROS_VERSION == 1" / "== 2" on the dependencies and on <build_type> in <export>.
    • CMakeLists.txt: keep the ROS1 lines byte-identical (no re-indentation), e.g. prepend the ROS2 build and wrap the original in else()/endif():
    if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
      cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
      project(foo)
      find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
      find_package(jsk_ros1_ros2_compat REQUIRED)
      jsk_ros1_ros2_compat_install_python(PROGRAMS scripts/foo_node.py)
      ament_package()
    else() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.3)
    project(foo)
    ...  # the ROS1 original, unchanged
    endif() # if("$ENV{ROS_VERSION}" EQUAL 2)
  • Python nodes call ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) instead of rospy.xxx(...), where node is None on ROS1 and the rclpy.node.Node on ROS2.

Python: jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat 

from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION

if __name__ == '__main__':
    node = ros_compat.init_node('foo')  # None on ROS1
    Foo(node)
    ros_compat.spin(node)
  ROS1 ROS2
get_param(node, '~name', default), has_param rospy.get_param declares a (dynamically typed) parameter
init_node(name, anonymous=False, multi_threaded=False) rospy.init_node, returns None rclpy.init() + a new node, returned (multi_threaded: see below)
spin(node), spin_once(node, timeout_sec), shutdown(node) (after an own while not is_shutdown(node) loop) rospy.spin, rospy.sleep, - spin_and_shutdown, rclpy.spin_once, cleanup
loginfo/logwarn/logerr/logdebug/logfatal(node, msg) rospy.log* node.get_logger().* (msg must be a str; node=None uses a logger named after the script)
loginfo/logwarn/logerr_throttle(node, period, msg), loginfo/logwarn/logerr_once(node, msg) like rospy.log*_throttle/_once like throttle_duration_sec=/once=True (per call site, done in compat)
create_publisher(node, topic, type, queue_size=1, latch=False) rospy.Publisher node.create_publisher (latch: transient-local QoS)
create_subscription(node, topic, type, cb, queue_size=None, latch=False) rospy.Subscriber (None: unbounded) node.create_subscription (None: depth 1; latch: transient-local QoS; ~foo -> ~/foo)
wait_for_service(node, name, type, timeout) (returns bool), set_param(node, name, value) rospy.wait_for_service, rospy.set_param a client’s wait_for_service, node.set_parameters
create_service, create_trigger_service, call_service, create_request/response, get_response_class (FooResponse(*values) on both) rospy.Service/ServiceProxy node.create_service/create_client
create_timer(node, period, cb) rospy.Timer node.create_timer (cb(None))
create_simple_action_client(node, name, type) actionlib.SimpleActionClient same subset over rclpy.action.ActionClient
create_simple_action_server(node, name, type, execute_cb) actionlib.SimpleActionServer same subset over rclpy.action.ActionServer
callback_group= of create_subscription/service/trigger_service/timer/simple_action_client/simple_action_server ignored (rospy runs each callback in its own thread) the rclpy callback group, e.g. ReentrantCallbackGroup() with a MultiThreadedExecutor
init_node(name, multi_threaded=True), for callbacks waiting for other callbacks (e.g. a service callback waiting for a topic) ignored (as above) create_* default to a ReentrantCallbackGroup and spin() uses a MultiThreadedExecutor
create_reconfigure_server(node, Config, cb, defaults) dynamic_reconfigure.server.Server parameters declared from defaults + on-set callback
now_sec, stamp_now, stamp_to_sec, duration_from_sec, sleep, Rate rospy.Time/Duration/... node.get_clock(), …
get_name, is_shutdown, on_shutdown, signal_shutdown rospy.* node name / rclpy context
create_tf_buffer_and_listener, create_tf_broadcaster tf2_ros tf2_ros with node
spin_and_shutdown(node, executor=None) - spin until SIGINT/SIGTERM/signal_shutdown, then clean up

Action types: pass FooAction/FooGoal on ROS1 and Foo/Foo.Goal on ROS2; timeouts are in seconds on both. actionlib/dynamic_reconfigure are imported lazily, so depend on them in your own package.

Packages outside jsk_common

jsk_ros1_ros2_compat is only released with jsk_common >= 3.0, which is not available for every ROS1 distro. Depend on it for ROS2 only and fall back to rospy when it can not be imported, listing just the functions you use:

<exec_depend condition="$ROS_VERSION == 2">jsk_ros1_ros2_compat</exec_depend>


try:
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat import rospy_rclpy_compat as ros_compat
    from jsk_ros1_ros2_compat.rospy_rclpy_compat import ROS_VERSION
except ImportError:
    # jsk_common < 3.0 has no jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, so this is ROS1 only:
    # forward ros_compat.xxx(node, ...) to rospy.xxx(...)
    import rospy
    ROS_VERSION = 1
    class ros_compat(object):
        get_param = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.get_param(*args, **kwargs))
        loginfo = staticmethod(lambda node, *args, **kwargs: rospy.loginfo(*args, **kwargs))

Or, to keep the original rospy code untouched for its ROS1 users, add a jsk_ros1_ros2_compat version next to it and choose by whether jsk_ros1_ros2_compat can be imported (not by ROS_VERSION):

Changelog for package jsk_ros1_ros2_compat

3.0.3 (2026-11-03)

  • Merge pull request #1835 from k-okada/ros-version-fallback-ament Fix ROS2 buildfarm binary jobs: ROS_VERSION without ros_environment, boost for jsk_topic_tools

  • Merge pull request #1834 from pazeshun/array-to-heatmap [jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_rosbag_tools] Add array heatmap tools with ROS 1 and ROS 2 support

  • Guess ROS_VERSION from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH when unset, depend on ros_environment The ROS2 binary jobs of the buildfarm failed at find_package(catkin): they install only the build dependencies, none of which pulls in ros_environment, so $ENV{ROS_VERSION} is empty and the fallback at the top of CMakeLists.txt chose ROS1.

    - package.xml: add a ROS2 buildtool_depend on ros_environment, which sets ROS_VERSION.

    - CMakeLists.txt: when ROS_VERSION is still unset, guess it from AMENT_PREFIX_PATH (bloom's ROS2 debian/rules passes it to cmake, setup.sh and colcon set the environment variable, catkin never does) instead of always assuming ROS1, and warn about it. jsk_tools had no fallback at all and gets the same block. Applies to jsk_ros1_ros2_compat, jsk_tools, jsk_topic_tools, jsk_common, jsk_data, jsk_rosbag_tools, dynamic_tf_publisher, audio_video_recorder and image_view2.
